# Secure Yourself & Your Family

We can all protect ourselves, our friends and our families from online threats. It’s fast. It’s easy.

## Four Easy Ways to Stay Safe Online

There are simple things we can do today that will help keep us much safer online. Digital crimes are happening every day, but by each of us doing our part—educating ourselves and paying attention—we can stay ahead of the game!

Four Easy Ways to Stay Safe Online ( [Audio Description](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/2023-09/SOW-Web-Page-Animation-Four-Easy-Ways-Audio-Description.pdf "Four Easy Ways to Stay Safe Online Audio Description"))

Let’s _Secure Our World_ through the simple behavior changes below that will make us all **MUCH SAFER.**

- [Recognize and report phishing](https://www.cisa.gov/avoid-phishing-attempts)

- [Use strong passwords](https://www.cisa.gov/use-strong-passwords)

- [Turn on multifactor authentication](https://www.cisa.gov/turn-mfa)

- [Update software](https://www.cisa.gov/update-software-promptly)


These steps will soon feel as natural as buckling our seat belts or brushing our teeth. Let’s share them with our children, parents and friends.

![decorative tipsheet icon](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/styles/16x9_medium/public/2023-08/tipsheet-bannerNEW.png?h=b53d1aba&itok=EFXluMD2)

## Four Easy Ways to Stay Safe Online Tip Sheet

Download the Secure Our World Four Easy Ways to Stay Safe Online Tip Sheet to share with friends and family.

[Download Tip Sheet](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/2024-09/Secure-Our-World-4-Easy-Ways-Stay-Safe-Online-Tip-Sheet.pdf "Secure Our World 4 Easy Ways to Stay Safe Online Tip Sheet")

## Four Easy Ways We Can Protect Ourselves Online

Online criminals look for easy targets, like people who don’t take basic precautions. If we take the following four steps, we won’t be as vulnerable to their deceptive tactics. It will be much harder to scam us or steal our information. Let’s start now.

![decorative photo of two people on a computer](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/styles/16x9_small/public/2023-09/SOW-Avoid-Phishing-Attempts.png?h=abce51c1&itok=zHtIJSVE)

### [Recognize & Report Phishing](https://www.cisa.gov/recognize-and-report-phishing)

Phishing is a tactic used to get us to open a malicious attachment or share personal information. Learn what to look for to avoid the "phish hook."

![decorative photo of people using a tablet](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/styles/16x9_small/public/2023-09/SOW-Secure-Family.png?h=abce51c1&itok=8cHPQpD_)

### [Use Strong Passwords](https://www.cisa.gov/use-strong-passwords)

Using strong passwords and a password manager are some easy ways to protect ourselves from someone logging into an account and stealing data or money.

![decorative photo of a person using the phone](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/styles/16x9_small/public/2023-09/SOW-Extra-MFA.png?h=abce51c1&itok=f94xrSd3)

### [Turn on MFA](https://www.cisa.gov/turn-mfa)

Multifactor authentication means using more than a password to access an app or account. With MFA, we might be asked to enter a text code or use a fingerprint. It alerts us and prevents others from accessing our accounts.

![decorative photo of a father and daughter looking at a tablet](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/styles/16x9_small/public/2023-09/SOW-Extra-Family2.png?h=abce51c1&itok=8JSX9NYU)

### [Update Software](https://www.cisa.gov/update-software)

Don't delay software updates. Flaws in software can give criminals access to files or accounts. Programmers fix these flaws as soon as they can, but we must install updates for the latest protection!
